issues: No integrity problems. The diff does no file or network I/O, pastes no coordinates and uses no labels. All randomness still comes from the seeded rng.

The force-directed initialisation has a bug: the wall term adds +0.5 both when c<0.1 and when c>0.9. Circles near the high walls (x or y above 0.9) are pushed outward instead of back in. np.clip hides this. The pairwise repulsion is also applied twice, once through forces[i] and again through forces[mask]. Both problems only change the starting points, which SLSQP and the repair step then process as before, so the measured result still means something. No veto.
The extra cost is a pure-Python 50x32 loop per restart. That is small, but it slightly cuts the number of restarts within the time budget.

Recomputed z: the gain is (-2.9253) - (-2.9243) = -0.0010, using a per-job sd of 0.0034. The standard error is 0.0034*sqrt(1/1+1/10) ≈ 0.00357, which gives z ≈ -0.28. The harness reports -0.265. The difference is within the rounding of the 4-decimal means: a difference anywhere from 0.00095 to 0.00105 gives |z| between 0.27 and 0.29. It could also come from a slightly different sd estimate. The sign agrees, and the result is a non-significant regression. Rejecting is correct.
Style: the change adds about 20 lines of messy code with no measured gain, so under the 'simpler is better' rule it should be rejected anyway.
